findings.title: Yiyip içmeyle bedene yerleşen göz aydınlığı
findings.claim: Yeme, içme ve gözü aydınlatma emirleri, rahatlığı beslenip sıvı alınmasıyla bedende yerleşen ve gözde görünür huzura dönen bir kabul olarak kurar.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for eating, drinking, and causative eye-comfort meet one another in a single restoration sequence. The reviewed wider provision connections at 3:37 and 77:43 and the maternal eye-comfort connections at 25:74 and 28:13 return through those focus words, making the sequence an embodied reception rather than an unanchored abstraction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the relief as something received and physically settled: nourishment enters, drinking completes the bodily provision, and settled sight names the resulting ease.
findings.containment: This deepens the plain commands to eat, drink, and let the eye be comforted. It does not turn عَيْنًا into a water-source noun or replace the idiomatic eye-comfort reading; the supplied water-related connections remain boundary evidence. The wider target ayat provide exact Arabic and reviewed relation notes but no target morphology, so the contextual extension stays qualified.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and cross-run support are trusted and exact, while the wider connection targets are supplied with Arabic and reviewed notes but without target-side morphology or lexical analysis.

branch_activations.carrier: The imperative كُلِى carries the ordinary act of consuming food.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The reviewed 3:37 connection supplies a parallel scene of Mary receiving divinely supplied provision, and the adjacent drinking imperative supplies a distinct paired restoration act.
branch_activations.activation: The wider provision scene returns to the focus eating carrier through Mary's embodied reception, while the adjacent drinking carrier keeps the contact attached to this ayah's restoration sequence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Eating here participates in a concrete provision that settles the body and makes the announced comfort inhabitable.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation is the restorative eating act in this scene; it does not activate the root's branches for wealth, speech, fire, or other figurative consumption.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: sıvı içme ve tek içimlik miktar
branch_activations.facet_statement: Su veya başka bir sıvı ağız yoluyla vücuda alınır.
branch_activations.carrier: The imperative ٱشْرَبِى carries the ordinary act of taking a liquid into the body.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The 3:37 provision connection and the 77:43 eat-and-drink consolation connection independently return nourishment and drinking to a bodily relief scene.
branch_activations.activation: Those wider provision scenes meet the focus drinking carrier and connect the liquid intake to the neighboring food command and eye-comfort result.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Drinking is part of the received, bodily completion of the comfort offered to Mary.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation concerns liquid intake as provision; it does not import a specific source, vessel, dose, or water-image into the focus phrase.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ettirgen anlatım, bir kişiye gözünü aydınlatacak sevinç ve doyum verilmesini bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The Form II imperative قَرِّى carries the causative eye-comfort idiom: a person is given settled, joyful sight.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The reviewed 25:74 and 28:13 connections explicitly return maternal receiving and eye-comfort to the child-reception scene, while the focus eating carrier supplies the local provision contact.
branch_activations.activation: The wider maternal eye-comfort scenes meet the focus causative idiom and make the comfort legible as the visible settling produced by received nourishment.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The eye-comfort phrase gathers the food and drink into a visible state of bodily and maternal ease.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation remains the established eye-comfort idiom and its received joy; it does not activate the separate coldness, spatial-settlement, or flowing-water branches.

findings.title: Susma ile işarete ve çocuğun sözüne açılan tanıklık
findings.claim: Rahman'a yöneltilen adak, insanlarla konuşmama biçiminde belirli ve süreli bir susmayı kurar; böylece Mary'nin insanlara vereceği tanıklık işaretlere ve çocuğun sonraki sözüne devredilmiş bir iletişim düzeninde görünür.
findings.mechanism: The vow carrier makes a self-binding act, the silence branch resolves the abstention domain through the following negated directed-speech verb, and the human and speech carriers define the social audience. Reviewed connections to sign-based silence at 3:41 and 19:11, to the child's speech at 3:46 and 5:110, and to vow fulfillment at 76:7 return through these focus carriers and change silence into a bounded communication arrangement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the silence as an authorized pause in public speech whose testimony arrives through gesture and the child's speech, while the ayah's literal instruction remains fully recoverable.
findings.containment: The plain reading remains Mary's instruction to say that she vowed to the Merciful and will not speak to any human today. The wider parallels add a delegated testimony pattern; they do not turn silence into loss of speech, erase Mary's prescribed utterance, or make every vow a speech vow. The target connections lack target-side morphology, so their contextual role remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and cross-run finding are trusted and exact; the wider connections supply explicit reviewed relations and target Arabic but not target morphology, so the global extension is qualified.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: insan türü ve bu türden bir kişi
branch_activations.facet_statement: İnsan türünü, insanların oluşturduğu topluluğu veya bu türün tek bir üyesini görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında adlandırır.
branch_activations.carrier: The indefinite human noun إِنسِيًّا names the human class and its individual members as the people from whom speech is withheld.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The reviewed 3:46 and 5:110 connections return the child's later speech explicitly to people, supplying a distinct human audience for the focus's no-speech clause.
branch_activations.activation: The human audience named by the carrier meets the wider child-to-people speech scenes, so the prohibition identifies the channel that the child's speech will later occupy.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The social-human object of silence becomes the receiving audience for testimony that appears through another speaker.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch establishes the human audience in this communication arrangement; it does not add an unseen-human contrast or a general claim about all human sociability.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel anlam, konuşma eylemini sürdürmeyip sessiz kalmaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: The noun صَوْمًا carries abstention from speaking once the following clause specifies human-directed speech.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The reviewed 3:41, 19:11, and 36:65 connections supply bounded silence accompanied by signs or a changed speaker.
branch_activations.activation: Those sign-and-speaker substitutions meet the focus silence carrier and make the abstention an intentional public-speech boundary.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Silence functions as a timed, authorized pause that opens another route for the scene's testimony.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation is chosen abstention from human speech; it does not claim loss of vocal capacity, physical muteness, or abstention from food.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: anlaşılır konuşma, hitap ve söz alışverişi
branch_activations.facet_statement: Birine hitap etme, onun sözüne karşılık verme ve bir kesintiden sonra yeniden karşılıklı konuşma, konuşma çekirdeğinin kişiler arası gerçekleşmeleridir.
branch_activations.carrier: The Form II verb أُكَلِّمَ is directed speech toward a human interlocutor, precisely the social act bounded by the vow.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The reviewed 3:46 and 5:110 connections give the child speech addressed to people, while 19:11 supplies the adjacent sign-based alternative during speech restraint.
branch_activations.activation: The directed-speech carrier meets those later speech and gesture roles, shifting the focus from generic quiet to management of who may speak to whom.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The vow reallocates public address: Mary's direct reply pauses while gesture and the child's directed speech carry the encounter.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch remains interpersonal speech and its addressee; it does not activate the separate word, wound, or merely technical speech branches.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Yükümlülük Tanrı'ya yöneltilen bir adak ya da kişinin kendi üzerine aldığı bağlayıcı söz olabilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The completed first-person verb نَذَرْتُ presents Mary's abstention as a self-binding vow directed to the Merciful.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The reviewed 76:7 and 22:29 connections treat vows as binding devotional acts whose fulfillment is due, supplying the wider obligation frame.
branch_activations.activation: The obligation frame meets the focus completed vow and explains why the speech pause has a stated duration and behavioral consequence rather than being a passing choice.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Silence becomes a declared devotional commitment that organizes the public encounter around an authorized transfer of testimony.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation concerns self-binding by vow in this scene; it does not import warning communication, injury compensation, or every conditional promise associated with the root.
